title: Customers from the US
prompt: List the `name` and `email` of every customer whose `country` is 'US'.
hints: Filter rows with WHERE.
String literals use single quotes.

title: Expensive electronics
prompt: Return `product_name` and `unit_price` for Electronics products costing more than 100, most expensive first.
hints: Combine two conditions with AND.
ORDER BY ... DESC sorts high to low.

title: Orders per status
prompt: Count the orders in each `status`. Return `status` and `order_count`.
hints: GROUP BY the column you want one row per value of.
COUNT(*) counts rows in each group.

title: Customers missing a signup date
prompt: Find the `name` of customers whose `signup_date` is not recorded.
hints: NULL is not equal to anything, even NULL.
Use IS NULL.

title: Category revenue potential
prompt: For each product `category`, return the number of products and the average `unit_price` rounded to 2 decimals. Name the columns `products` and `avg_price`.
hints: Use COUNT(*) and AVG().
ROUND(x, 2).

title: Customer names with order dates
prompt: Return `name` and `order_date` for every completed order (`status = 'completed'`).
hints: Join orders to customers on customer_id.
INNER JOIN keeps only matching rows.

title: Customers who never ordered
prompt: Return the `name` of customers who have placed no orders at all.
hints: LEFT JOIN keeps every customer; unmatched rows have NULL order columns.
Or use NOT EXISTS.

title: Revenue per order
prompt: Compute the revenue of each order as the sum of `quantity * unit_price * (1 - discount)`. Return `order_id` and `revenue` rounded to 2 decimals.
hints: Join order_items to products.
Aggregate per order_id.

title: Big spenders (HAVING)
prompt: Return `customer_id` for customers whose completed orders total more than 1000 in revenue (quantity * unit_price * (1 - discount)). Also return the `revenue` rounded to 2 decimals.
hints: Filter rows (WHERE) before grouping, filter groups (HAVING) after.
You need three tables.

title: Above-average salaries
prompt: List `emp_name` and `salary` of employees earning more than the company-wide average salary.
hints: A scalar subquery can return the average.
(SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees)

title: Above their department average
prompt: List `emp_name`, `department` and `salary` for employees earning more than the average of their own department (use a correlated subquery).
hints: The inner query refers to the outer row's department.
Alias the outer table, e.g. e1.

title: Order size buckets (CASE)
prompt: For each product return `product_name` and a `tier`: 'premium' if unit_price >= 300, 'standard' if >= 50, otherwise 'budget'.
hints: CASE WHEN ... THEN ... ELSE ... END.
Order the WHEN branches from most to least specific.

title: Handling NULLs
prompt: Return `name` and the signup year of every customer; for customers without a signup date show 0 as the year. Name the columns `name` and `signup_year`.
hints: EXTRACT(year FROM date) or year(date).
COALESCE replaces NULL.

title: Customers with orders or accounts (UNION)
prompt: Return the distinct customer ids that either placed an order or hold an account. Single column `customer_id`.
hints: UNION removes duplicates; UNION ALL keeps them.
Select the same number of columns from both sides.

title: Latest order per customer
prompt: For each customer who has ordered, return `customer_id`, `order_id` and `order_date` of their most recent order.
hints: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date DESC).
Keep rows where the number is 1.

title: Rank salaries per department
prompt: Return `emp_name`, `department`, `salary` and `salary_rank` using DENSE_RANK within each department (highest salary = 1).
hints: PARTITION BY department, ORDER BY salary DESC.
DENSE_RANK has no gaps after ties.

title: Top 2 earners per department
prompt: Return `emp_name`, `department` and `salary` for the two highest-paid employees in each department. Break salary ties with ROW_NUMBER ordered by emp_name.
hints: Rank in a subquery or CTE, then filter.
Window functions can't be used directly in WHERE.

title: Previous order gap (LAG)
prompt: For every order return `order_id`, `customer_id`, `order_date` and `days_since_prev` - days since the same customer's previous order (NULL for their first). Use LAG and date arithmetic.
hints: LAG(order_date) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date).
Subtracting two DATEs in DuckDB gives an integer number of days.

title: CTE: customers above average spend
prompt: Using CTEs, compute total completed-order revenue per customer, then return `customer_id` and `revenue` (2 decimals) for customers whose revenue is above the average of all those customers.
hints: First CTE: revenue per customer.
Second step compares with AVG(revenue) from the CTE.

title: Management hierarchy (recursive CTE)
prompt: Use a recursive CTE to list every employee under Priya Nair (emp_id 1) directly or indirectly. Return `emp_name` and `depth` (direct reports have depth 1).
hints: WITH RECURSIVE, anchor = direct reports, recursive step joins on manager_id.
Increase depth by 1 each level.

title: Running total of monthly sales
prompt: For the EMEA region return `month`, `revenue` and `running_total` (cumulative revenue ordered by month) from `monthly_sales`.
hints: SUM(...) OVER (ORDER BY month) accumulates.
Filter region = 'EMEA'.

title: Month-over-month growth
prompt: For each region and month return `region`, `month`, `revenue` and `growth_pct` = percentage change versus the previous month in the same region, rounded to 1 decimal (NULL for the first month).
hints: LAG(revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY month).
(current - prev) / prev * 100.

title: 3-month moving average
prompt: Return `region`, `month` and `moving_avg` - the average revenue over the current and previous two months within each region, rounded to 2 decimals.
hints: Use a window frame: ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW.
Partition by region.

title: Share of regional revenue
prompt: Return `region`, `month` and `pct_of_region` = the month's revenue as a percentage of that region's total revenue, rounded to 1 decimal.
hints: SUM(revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY region) is the denominator.
Multiply by 100.0 to avoid integer division.

title: Conversion funnel
prompt: From `web_events` compute, per `event_type` in ('login','view','add_to_cart','purchase'), the number of distinct users reaching it. Return `event_type` and `users`.
hints: COUNT(DISTINCT user_id).
Filter the four event types.

title: Sessionise events
prompt: A new session starts when a user's gap since their previous event exceeds 30 minutes. Return `user_id` and `sessions` - the number of sessions per user. (Gaps use LAG; count session starts.)
hints: Compute previous event time with LAG per user.
A row starts a session if prev is NULL or the gap is greater than 30 minutes.
Then SUM a 0/1 flag per user.

title: Deduplicate staging customers
prompt: `stg_customers` holds several versions of the same customer. Keep only the latest row per `customer_id` (by `updated_at`). Return `customer_id`, `name`, `email`. Ties on updated_at don't occur for the latest rows.
hints: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY updated_at DESC).
Filter rn = 1.

title: Find duplicate keys (data quality check)
prompt: Return the `customer_id` values that appear more than once in `stg_customers` along with `copies` (the row count).
hints: GROUP BY the key, HAVING COUNT(*) > 1.

title: Point-in-time SCD2 lookup
prompt: Using the SCD2 dimension `dim_customer_scd2`, enrich each `fact_sales` row with the customer's `city` as it was on `sale_date` (valid_from <= sale_date <= valid_to). Return `sale_id` and `city`.
hints: Join on customer_id AND a date-range condition.
BETWEEN valid_from AND valid_to.

title: Current dimension rows only
prompt: Return the current version (is_current = true) of each customer from `dim_customer_scd2`: `customer_id` and `city`.
hints: Filter on the is_current flag.

title: Incremental load: new and changed rows
prompt: An incremental job loads rows from `stg_customers` with `updated_at` later than the watermark '2024-02-01 00:00:00'. Return `customer_id` and the `max_updated` timestamp per customer for those rows.
hints: Filter updated_at > watermark.
GROUP BY customer_id with MAX(updated_at).

title: Detect suspicious transactions
prompt: Flag debit transactions where the absolute amount exceeds 5000. Return `txn_id`, `account_id`, `amount`.
hints: Debits are negative amounts here; use ABS().
Filter txn_type = 'debit'.

title: Account balance reconciliation
prompt: Reconcile accounts: for each account compute `txn_total` = SUM(amount) of its transactions. Return `account_id`, `txn_total`, only for accounts with at least one transaction.
hints: Aggregate transactions by account_id.

title: Filter early with EXISTS
prompt: Return customer `name`s who placed at least one cancelled order. Use EXISTS rather than joining and deduplicating (an EXISTS semi-join stops at the first match).
hints: EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id AND ...).

title: Select only the columns you need
prompt: A report only needs `order_id` and `order_date` of completed orders from March 2024. Write it selecting just those columns (avoid SELECT *). Date range: 2024-03-01 up to but excluding 2024-04-01.
hints: Prefer half-open ranges: >= start AND < next_start.
Columnar engines read only the columns you name.

title: Aggregate before joining
prompt: Return each customer's `name` and `orders` count by aggregating `orders` first in a subquery/CTE and joining the small result to `customers` (including customers with zero orders, count 0).
hints: Aggregate orders by customer_id in a CTE.
LEFT JOIN customers to it and COALESCE the count.
